chunks: And by this chain, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said: I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Muhzim al-Asadi entered upon him.

He said: Inform me, may I be your ransom, when is this affair that we are waiting for? It has been delayed too long. He (peace be upon him) said: O Muhzim, the time-keepers have lied, the hasteners will perish, and the Muslims will be saved, and they will return to us.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَعْجِلُونَ: The hasteners (those impatient for the reappearance)
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُونَ: The Muslims (the faithful who are saved)
key_terms.الْوَقَاتُونَ: The time-keepers (those who assign specific times)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the time-keepers, hasteners, and Muslims regarding the Imam's reappearance?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the theological distinction between mere chronological speculation (*al-waqatun*) and patient expectation (*al-intizar*) during the Occultation. It underscores the Shia doctrine that ultimate authority and return belong to the Imams, warning against the spiritual peril of impatience while affirming the salvation of those who remain steadfast in their faith.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 413 - It is narrated from the same chains from Abdur Rahman bin Kathir that he said: I was with Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) when Muhzim Asadi entered

and asked: May I be sacrificed on you, please tell me when the reappearance is? It has been delayed too much.” Abu Abdullah (a.s) said: “O Muhzim, the ill-wishers have told lies, the hasteners will perish and the believers will be saved and will be with us.”
